column1: # Capacity and cadence numbers written in Rust. `source` is either the reading the
# value is derived from or the reason it is a bound; `unreviewed` is debt, not an
# answer. Regenerate with COGNEVA_CAPACITY_REGISTRY_WRITE=1 cargo test -p cogneva

column5: note
seconds of the device's own write allowed to pile before background writeback starts
seconds of unflushed write before a writer is made to wait for its own writeback
a cap on the derived watermarks; keeps a fast device from holding the whole node's RAM dirty
one turn's share: long enough to store a payload, short enough not to wedge the turn
safety threshold so a still-draining process is not robbed; nothing waits on it
policy split: half the window is kept for task input and later turns
identical events inside one second run one action; cog-core's dedup_window_secs default spells the same 1
a default wait for one hook action; cog-core's hook_timeout_secs and HookDef::timeout() spell the same 30
how far back the ceiling looks; older runs describe another workload
a batching choice; the flush deadline is what bounds the wait
flush deadline for buffered events; the batch size of 16 is the other half of the batching
sits just above the 0.70-0.72 baseline measured on the main pod on 2026-10-24
one decision below the chart's 0.81 near-limit alert, so the alert reports a failure
a default wait inside a turn, long enough for a peer's run and no longer
the cap that keeps a peer's silence from becoming an unbounded wait
enough synthetic names that an accidental alphabetical hash order is negligible
roughly the payload a tool result carries when it still fits a turn
one turn's share: enough for a bounded payload, short enough not to wedge the turn
a page that has not started answering by then will not make the turn useful
past this the answer is a document, and a document belongs in the archive
ceiling on hits; every hit is context every later turn pays for
room for a browser to start, run scripts and settle; the fetch deadline is too short
the point past which the slowest metasearch engine is not worth the turn
how long a fetched key set is reused; bounds how long a rotated-away key is still accepted
twice the largest TokenBudget threshold the shipped configurations declare (100000 in all three carriers); the estimator saturates here, and a gate test keeps every declared threshold below it
the first repair is what lets feedback be acted on at all, the second absorbs a first rewrite that was itself rejected; past that the feedback is unchanged, so repeating it cannot buy another outcome
declared file count at which a change is too big for the lightest topology — one above the shortcut's ceiling of 3
declared diff size at which a change is too big for the lightest topology; three times the shortcut's 40 leaves a band where declared size alone does not decide
design rule with nothing measured yet: score below it takes the cheaper decomposition, and on the boundary the roundtable wins because the decision is uncertain
files a request may name and still be the shortcut's own work
diff lines an attached change may declare and still be the shortcut's own work
ceiling on the paced backoff so a paused squad is not silent longer than a minute; the known cost of the last paced round is recorded above it rather than folded into the number
floor before a median is this workload's history rather than noise
cargo's profile level, then the deps/incremental level that can be dropped
a 5 GiB claim less the co-tenants measured by hand; the auto cap can replace it
series cap; everything past it is folded into one other series by size
floor; a metadata walk over hundreds of thousands of entries gains nothing fresher
an hour, matching the hand readings on record and the length of a real build
headroom over the measured peak so the next repeat build is not instantly over cap
shared cadence so readings from different walkers stay comparable
no fresher than the 30s scrape interval; a cheap metadata walk gains nothing
the token lifetime's default; cog-auth's JwtConfig::default spells the same 15 separately
hourly against a 24h Gitee token, leaving room for several failed renewals
one window shared by the ready sweeper and the publisher's stall check
per-consumer quiet period: one round trip when idle, prompt wake when not
a drain read; the entries it waits for are already in the stream
three renewal ticks at lease/3, so two may be missed before another process judges it gone
character ceiling because names come from the document and multiply the length
names spelled out before the rest are counted; keeps one alert row readable
long enough for a path or an upstream message to survive truncation, short enough that a label value stays a label value
depth at which a bounded event stream pushes back; a default, not a measured queue length
ten minutes covers a build or a long model call and still shows a stopped owner inside the same working session
fifteen minutes is enough for the two parties to finish the move they signed, short enough that a signature nobody applied is visible inside the same session
with the timestamp and random segments alongside it the whole raw id stays far below NAME_MAX, while the prefix still shows where an entry came from
past six characters a trailing .foo reads as a sentence fragment rather than a file type
one letter is the shape of an abbreviation (e.g, i.e), not of a file type anybody ships
a judgement is made against a handful of artifacts; a longer list is a corpus, and a corpus belongs on the material side where it can be paged
fits a URI with a query string, not a document in the field whose job is to point at one
a subject line; over-length is refused at submission rather than truncated, because a cut subject is the submitter's words with the reason removed
these fields are inlined into the goal and copied into every later change, so the bound is on the submission, not on the row as stored
at most five test names in a verdict; the rest are counted, not listed
a gate two orders above normal call density; it only bites in a refusal storm
floor when a refusal states no wait; three orders above the measured 0.7ms fast failure
above the ~4min window flip seen and below a 45min pod's life; past it the call is refused, not waited
below this a `data:` string is prose mentioning the word, not an attachment
default cadence; the shared floor is applied where the interval is read
one working day; a plan unread longer is no longer the plan about to be read
past a few thousand entries the listing costs more than it tells either reader
below this the plan could expire between being displayed and clicked
a couple of kilobytes name the file; the call costs more with every byte
past a few dozen files the rule table, not the files, is the subject
long enough for a slow upstream, short enough not to hang on a silent channel
seed; applies only until the first observed move of main, then the fetch period follows that
seed; applies only until a reclamation pass has been timed, then the interval follows the pass
policy ceiling when the deployment names none; the disk measurement can still lower it
seed; applies only until two trees exist to give an arrival interval

multiple of the slowest git command that has completed here
a directory-name limit, not a capacity of this machine

floor under the pass-duration derivation; also the pace the loop wakes and beats at
floor under the arrival-rate derivation, before two trees exist
room the git commands writing while the cap is reached need
the A2A specification's default page_size when the caller names none
the A2A specification's page_size ceiling
one default page of conversation lines; the store keeps far more and the caller may ask for it
longest a request may hold a connection waiting for an agent's answer, set below the idle bound of the proxies in front
failed attempts per identifier inside the window before the endpoint answers 429
the sliding window the failed-attempt count is kept in, so an attacker's budget is per five minutes
intent classification is a one-word answer; past this the backend is struggling and the plain chat path takes over
connecting is fast or the backend is the problem, and the failover pool is what handles a slow one
how many turns fit in one request, not how many are stored — the record is trimmed by its own bound in the store
matches the upstream's own in-stream cap; only an idle gap beyond it aborts a reasoning turn
each listed report costs one body read to name its dataset, so the cap bounds the reads; the untrimmed total is reported so the caller sees a prefix
total wall for one clone/fetch/push; the stall judgement cannot catch a remote that keeps printing progress and never ends
silence that marks a transfer dead; --progress writes at second granularity, so silence is no progress, while a slow link still makes progress
base of the circuit-breaker probe backoff: consecutive failures retreat exponentially from this cadence
a mirror's last successful fetch must be this recent to serve as a baseline; the same number is the oldest a fallback baseline may be
lowest the deployment may set the operation timeout to; below it a large legitimate fetch is cut
lowest the deployment may set the stall judgement to, so a healthy transfer is never killed for being quiet
newer residue may belong to a live transfer (progress updates by the second, locks live less than a request); only clearly stale files are a dead process's
probe budget for one channel's handshake, not a channel's request budget — exceeding it means the channel is unavailable now
how long a measured channel verdict stands: longer than the circuit-breaker probe cadence, short enough that a torn-down wall shows within minutes
one network-profile signal probe, at the same order as the bootstrap's short probes: reachable, not how fast
issued-at is backdated by a minute so clock drift against GitHub cannot make the token not-yet-valid
installation token is refreshed this long before its expiry, so a request never carries one about to lapse
one page of outstanding rows; the total comes from the census, not from the page
refused principles returned by one read; both totals are taken before the truncation, so the page never doubles as the count
rows read to compute the totals, bounded by how many principles one deployment could ever have refused
widest history a caller may ask for in one read
moves returned by one history; they come newest first, so the bound drops the oldest and the question is how this got here
prefix examined before a file is called binary, and the same files are never returned in full
one directory listing; a tree of millions of files must not fill a response
matches returned when the caller names no limit
search answers synchronously, so it walks a bounded number of files before it stops looking
widest page of matches a caller may ask for
widest answer assembled over HTTP rather than an internal candidate window; the same ceiling the wiki search applies
a listing costs one store read per id, so the cap bounds the reads; the untrimmed total is reported so a prefix is visible
lifetime of the signed URL for stored bytes: long enough for the request that asked, short enough that a working link does not circulate
the cluster verdict only asks whether anything fires, so one row settles it however much is firing
a reading that cannot answer in five seconds is already the answer; a failed query reads as no reading and never as zero
one git action on a small local repository; slower than a poll cycle means it is wedged
most log rows returned
changes returned by one status read
keeps a pathological line count from filling the byte cap with tiny lines; the byte cap is the primary bound
wider than a changelog line and narrower than an article; the byte cap beside it is what really bounds a diff
paths one commit may name
a face probe is a max_tokens=1 ping, and losing a face is a slow event; this interval is also the eligibility window, so a ten-day-old answer cannot admit traffic today
upstream error excerpt: the truncation point is chosen so the vendor's own error-type marker (access_terminated_error) survives, because termination classification reads it
a month of history: shorter is skewed by one unusually cheap batch, longer carries shapes from before a config or prompt change
median would leave half the tasks unable to reserve for themselves, which is the shape of opening a window and cutting it in two; the 75th percentile fits most tasks whole
a definition, not a measurement: 24x3600, with the day boundary being UTC's rather than this deployment's
a cap on git-show subprocesses per red revision; the logs named two or three paths in practice
only the six newest attachments per intent reach the judge
how often the wait loop re-asks for the verdict; a cadence, not a reading
the task's kill time, twenty seconds past the poller's own give-up so the two end together
how long one round blocks before falling back to the local heuristic
room for apply, workspace tests and an eval A/B in one sandbox task
how many sandbox validations one instance runs at once
the page size a provider listing asks for; the provider spells the same 100 per call
the longest header this crate writes plus the fifty characters a goal's first line may fill
five failed jobs' logs per run, each already tailed to 16 KiB
the forward channel's depth; routing.rs holds a second copy of the same 64
one deployed 64k agent window of transcript; the raw layer no longer trims to it
four doublings from 500 ms cap the wait at 8 s inside the 120 s retry window
the first retry delay; doubling from here keeps asking during a create storm
the same 300 as cog-core's DEFAULT_SCAN_INTERVAL_SECS, so two processes reporting one claim are equally fresh and the older one's number does not read as growth
a scan walks every directory below the root, so a faster cadence only keeps the disk busy
below the settle floor the hold only re-reads one window, while the pod replacement it waits out takes minutes
scrape intervals dominate freshness, so a faster poll burns Prometheus CPU without showing anything sooner
kubelet refreshes the mounted document on its own sync period; a shorter window would read the same stale document twice and call a rollout a permanent gap
slower than the claim scan because an image tree is much larger and changes on the scale of pulls, not of a workload writing a file
fastest re-walk a deployment may ask for, bounded because the walk costs what the node holds
enough of a Prometheus message to recognise the cause, not enough to flood an alert row; a Prometheus message embeds the whole match group
a property of the reading rather than a knob: one hour keeps a quiet window a meaningful rate and a shift in where tokens go visible the same day, and a different window would be a different series
the same 60 seconds the WebUI's useNotifications polls at: faster is spin because the browser cannot see it sooner, slower lights the bell a full tick late
long enough that an owner collecting through a blocking wait() always wins the race, short enough that a wedged sweep is visible within one scrape interval
the same closed hour the usage rollup folds, so a verdict cell and the spend it judges are keyed identically and need no mapping
patterns older than a month are expired even under the size cap
the table is truncated at this many patterns after sorting by success and recency
slow enough for a table that changes a few times a day; the liveness alert uses 6x this period
far above any real firing set; a read that fills it reports itself as not a census
maintenance cadence, not arrival rate; the alert uses 6x this and a compile-time assert ties the sweep
one maintenance tick's slice, so a pass cannot hold the owner lease past its cadence
a page under the 146-event longest run, so the read must page rather than stop
questions to a local repo take tens of ms; this is the stalled-mount ceiling, not a latency reading
per-step ceiling so one hung agent or store cannot stall the round; it also feeds the declared work bound
pass cadence; it only has to stay slower than the 30s ballot close interval
test fixture: a ten-minute idle threshold, the core default in milliseconds
three stall windows of backlog are tolerated before the sweep re-arms the task
wider than the one-shot corpus intake, so one pass folds the list whole

four 256-event rings' worth, so it fills only when the account has been unwritable for long

a process-wide in-flight ceiling; enough that a 90-minute task cannot stall recovery

the length of a UTC day; a definition, not a measured allowance

the point past which a reply is lost rather than late, not a latency target

one page of waiting approvals per round; the backlog advances a page at a time

margin over the longest legal build or test hold, so a legal wait is never refused
damping window so the persisted bound does not chase every sample; a build lasts tens of minutes
ring depth for a consumer ticking every few minutes; drops are counted, not lost
sits above the worst one build has measured and below two; a seven-day reading
how promptly a waiter rechecks a freed slot; builds last minutes, so this is only responsiveness
longer than any asker's own round, so a grievance outlives the call that raised it
turns a walk stands down before taking the field; a policy for two failure directions

extra wait past the Job's own deadline for the controller to judge it and write status
one command per change spends the build budget; a test holds the call-site count
hung-rustfmt ceiling; formatting the workspace takes seconds, not a minute
a ceiling two orders above the 3.7s and 1.6s measured once; a hung command must not hold the slot
clippy plus two test runs spend the test budget; a test holds the call-site count
floor on the convergence cadence; below it an apply has not landed before the next round
in-process attempt window; it answers for this process's life, not for all of history
how much evidence a learning may carry; a spend for the next attempt, not a storage limit

wall for the strip hop inside the build stage; it is a separate hop so hitting it is not fatal to the build next to it
the text comes from the cluster, so its length cannot be the cluster's to decide: it ends up in logs, termination messages and failure records
one budget used at both ends — the ask's own timeout here and the Job's activeDeadlineSeconds there — because bounding only one end leaves the other nominal

actions the pattern detector can see; a fixed depth, not a reading
